hints: Focus on what is being plotted. The y-axis is a reactant, $\text{MnO}_4^-$, so its concentration must start high and fall to near zero.
Notice the reaction is described as very slow at first, so the initial gradient of the concentration-time graph must be almost flat (close to zero).
Consider that $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ product speeds the reaction up, then reactants run out, so the fall starts slow, gets steep, then flattens again.
walkthrough:
**Identify reactant or product**

We are following $\text{MnO}_4^-$, which is a reactant. Its concentration starts at its initial value and must decrease as it is used up.

$$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 10\text{CO}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Spot the autocatalysis**

The product $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ catalyses the reaction. This is autocatalysis. At time zero there is no $\text{Mn}^{2+}$, so the rate is very slow.

Rate is proportional to gradient, so slow rate means shallow gradient at the start.

**Build the S-shaped fall**

As a little $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ forms, the rate increases, so the graph gets steeper in the middle. Finally, $\text{MnO}_4^-$ and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ are used up, so the rate slows again and the curve flattens toward zero.

That gives a high to low, slow-steep-slow curve, which is graph B.

options.A: Incorrect. This curve rises from zero, so it shows a product forming, not a reactant being used up. In fact it is the correct shape for the autocatalysed formation of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$, the opposite of what is asked.
options.B: Correct. Concentration of $\text{MnO}_4^-$ starts high and falls. The fall is slow at first (flat), then fast as $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ catalyst builds up (steep), then slow again as reactants are consumed (flat). This S-shaped decrease is classic for autocatalysis.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the normal shape for a reaction that is fastest at the start and then slows down. Here the start is very slow because no catalyst $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is present yet, so the initial steep drop is wrong.
options.D: Incorrect. This curve rises quickly then levels off, which describes formation of a product in a normal uncatalysed reaction. We need a fall in reactant concentration with an autocatalytic slow start.
